A.title: Weaver's Count
A.text: Forty looms in this hall and thirty-nine weavers still working. The fortieth chair is warm. Do not sit in it.

Y.title: Tied and Tagged
Y.text: A bundle wrapped so tight the cord has cut into the cloth. A tag reads: the thing inside is the weaver's. Cut the knots in the order they were tied, or the web notices.

R.title: Weavers' Thread-Sense
R.text: Hold one thread loosely. Feel it hum when a spider crosses the far end. The weavers learned to feel the whole web through a single strand. Stand still and let the threads tell you where things are.

G.title: Spindle Song
G.text: Turn left, turn right, draw the thread. A skipping rhyme scratched on a spindle. The last verse says: step on silk and the silk steps back.

M.title: The Spindle Speaks
M.text: If a spindle hums at night, someone is walking the web. The hum gets louder as they get closer. Spindlers who ignored it were found wrapped and standing upright.

O.title: Knotted for Luck
O.text: Weavers tied their worries into the thread and sent them down the hall. I untied one and nothing happened. I am still waiting.

U.title: First Cloth
U.text: The first thing woven here was a flag. After it, a shroud. After that, they stopped keeping count of what they made. Mo said cloth outlasts the hand.

X.title: The Hub of the Web
X.text: All the threads in these halls run to one place. Pull one and the others move. A hunter's mark beside the loom says: cut the weakest and leave the rest.
